## The Flox way: an ephemeral environment in a temp directory

Flox always needs a `.flox` directory to hold the environment — there's no truly "directoryless" run. But you can keep it out of your project entirely by creating it in a throwaway temp dir, running your command with `flox activate -- <cmd>`, and deleting it. Nothing lands in your project and nothing is installed system-wide.

### One-liner (throwaway, self-cleaning)

```bash
d=$(mktemp -d) && flox init -d "$d" -q && flox install -d "$d" -q jq && flox activate -d "$d" -- jq --version; rm -rf "$d"
```

Replace `jq --version` with whatever you actually need to run. The `-d "$d"` points every Flox command at the temp dir, `-- <cmd>` runs the command without dropping you into a subshell, and `rm -rf "$d"` removes the whole thing (env included) afterward.

### Same thing, readable

```bash
# 1. Make a throwaway directory for the env
tmp=$(mktemp -d)

# 2. Create + populate it (nothing touches your project)
flox init -d "$tmp" -q
flox install -d "$tmp" -q jq

# 3. Run your one-off command
flox activate -d "$tmp" -- jq '.foo' somefile.json

# 4. Delete the env and temp dir
rm -rf "$tmp"
```

- `-d <path>` / `--dir` makes Flox

The Flox way to run a one-off command from a CLI tool you don't have installed — without an environment and without a `.flox/` directory — is **`flox run`**. It pulls the package straight from the catalog for that single invocation (think `npx`, but for any catalog package).

## Solution

```bash
flox run -p jq -- jq '.foo' data.json
```

That's the whole thing — no `flox init`, no `flox install`, no `.flox/` directory created. Flox fetches `jq` from the catalog, runs your command in an ephemeral context, and leaves nothing behind in your project.

## Anatomy of the command

```
flox run -p jq -- jq '.foo' data.json
         │  │     │  └────────────── the command to run (with its own args)
         │  │     └──── separates flox's flags from your command — always include it
         │  └──── the catalog package to make available
         └──── run subcommand
```

- **`-p <pkg>` is required** — it names the catalog package to provision. (If you're unsure of the catalog name, `flox search jq` / `flox show jq` first; names usually match nixpkgs but not always.)
